title: CoderHelm plugin manifest
description: The plugin.yaml file at the root of a CoderHelm plugin repo. A plugin is text plus approved tools: its behavior comes from its agents and skills, and this file declares what it may touch.

$schema.description: Optional. Point editors at this schema for completion and checks.

name.description: The plugin's id. Lowercase letters, digits and `-`. A marketplace plugin is namespaced by its publisher, as `publisher/name`.

version.description: The plugin's version, in semantic versioning (`MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`). Installs are pinned by content hash, so the version is a label for people; raise it whenever you publish.

description.description: One line saying what the plugin does. Shown on the install screen and in the marketplace.

skills.description: Paths or globs of the plugin's skills, relative to the repo root. Skills use the same SKILL.md format as skill repos.

agents.description: Paths or globs of the plugin's agents. Each agent file is Markdown with frontmatter; its body is the agent's instructions.

settings.description: Values a team fills in when it installs the plugin. Values live in the team's settings, never in the package.

tools.description: Every tool the plugin's agents may call. A tool that is not listed here does not exist for a plugin run.

triggers.description: What starts a run of the plugin.

outputs.description: What a run produces. Drafts wait in the review queue; a publish output sends an approved draft out through a consequential tool.

budget.description: A monthly token limit for this plugin, checked alongside the team's own limits. A team can lower it but not raise it above the team limit.

monthly_tokens.description: New tokens (input plus output) the plugin may use per calendar month (UTC). Omit for no plugin limit; the team limits still apply.

settingKey.description: Lowercase letters, digits and `_`, starting with a letter.

type.description: `string` is one line, `text` is several. `secret` is sealed and never shown to a model. `connection` asks the team to connect an account (OAuth or a key).

label.description: The field's label on the install screen. Defaults to the key.

required.description: The plugin cannot run until this is set.

default.description: The value used when the team leaves the field empty. Not allowed for `secret` and `connection`.

provider.description: For a `connection`: how the account is connected.

scopes.description: For an `oauth2` connection: the scopes asked for. Adding a scope in a new version needs an admin's approval.

per_user.description: For a `connection`: each person connects their own account instead of one shared team account.

sensitive.description: Seal the value and keep it out of every prompt. Always true for `secret` and `connection`.

risk.description: `read` only looks. `write` changes something that a person can still review, such as a draft in a CMS. `consequential` reaches people or money (publish, send, post, pay) and runs only after an approval.

toolRef.description: Tools from a connection the team has, such as an MCP server from Connections.

ref.description: `mcp:<id>` for a connection's MCP server, or `tool:<name>` for one of the team's approved tools.

allow.description: Tool names or `*` globs from that server the plugin may call. Everything else on the server is hidden from the run.

risk.description: The highest risk among the allowed tools. CoderHelm checks each tool's own risk and refuses an install that understates it.

pattern.description: A regular expression the whole value must match.

example.description: A real value, used when the tool is checked before approval.

httpTool.description: A tool the plugin defines itself: one HTTP request with typed inputs.

name.description: Lowercase letters, digits and `_`. Agents call the tool by this name, and it must not clash with a name in an `allow` list.

description.description: When an agent should use the tool.

url.description: HTTPS only. `{input}` and `{settings.key}` are filled in and URL-encoded.

connection.description: The `connection` setting whose credentials sign the request. The model never sees them.

headers.description: Extra headers. Values may use `{settings.key}`; `Authorization` comes from the connection.

body.description: A JSON body template. String values may use `{input}` and `{settings.key}`.

inputs.description: Typed inputs the agent fills in. Values are checked against their type before the request is made.

manualTrigger.description: A person starts a run from the dashboard with a short brief.

form.description: The brief form: each field is a type, or a list of choices.

cron.description: Five-field cron: minute, hour, day of month, month, day of week.

timezone.description: An IANA time zone, such as `America/New_York`.

releaseTrigger.description: Runs when a release is published on a connected GitHub repo. The run receives the release notes CoderHelm wrote.

repos.description: Only these repos (`owner/name`). Omit for every repo the team connected.

kinds.description: The kinds of draft a run may save.

via.description: The name of a `consequential` tool from `tools` that sends an approved draft out.

role.description: Who may approve: a role, or an approver group the team creates for this plugin.

min.description: How many different approvers are needed.

approval.description: The approval a draft needs before it is published. The person who asked for the run can never approve its output.
